newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arabs, Israelis protest against settlement plan.
newsitem.headline: Arabs, Israelis protest against settlement plan.

text.p: Hundreds of Palestinians and Israelis gathered in an Arab neighbourhood in East Jerusalem on Friday to protest against plans to build 132 Jewish homes there.
"There will not be peace between us and the Israelis...if a settlement is established here," Faisal al-Husseini, the PLO's top official in Jerusalem, told the crowd.

Ahmed Korei, speaker of the Palestinian legislature, said Palestinians were prepared to confront Israel "by all means" if the construction went ahead in Ras al-Amoud, outside the walls of the Old City of Jerusalem.
Yossi Sarid, a left-wing Israeli legislator, said a Jewish neighbourhood in Ras al-Amoud, home to 11,000 Palestinians, would be like "a bone in the throat".

Israel's Jerusalem District Planning Commisission decided last week to approve plans to construct the houses on a 3.5 acre (1.3 hectare) plot which a Miami-based Jewish businessman says he owns. The claim is disputed by Palestinian officials.
Ground-breaking is conditional on approval by Israel's interior minister, who has said he would first consult with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
The right-wing Israeli leader has so far balked at establishing new settlements although he has approved thousands of new homes for existing ones.
Palestinians say the construction aims at blocking the possibility of returning East Jerusalem to Arab sovereignty in a permanent peace settlement.

Israel captured East Jerusalem along with the rest of the West Bank in the 1967 Middle East war. It views all of Jerusalem as its eternal and indivisible capital. The PLO wants to make East Jerusalem capital of a future Palestinian state.
